disposition_reason: Legal review of Indian heavy-metal regulation; its only cocoa-specific limit is copper in cocoa powder 70 ppm (copper is not a tracked analyte). It restates residual 'food not specified' limits (lead 2.5 ppm, cadmium 1.5 ppm) from the FSS (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations 2011 as secondary text.
disposition_locator: Section III, body text p. 1334-1335 and Table 1

study.material_scope: secondary legal review; no tracked-analyte cocoa limit

unresolved: The FSSAI primary regulation (2011 as amended 7 Aug 2020, in force 1 July 2021 per the review) was not read; whether residual Pb 2.5 / Cd 1.5 ppm limits still apply to cocoa and chocolate in India is unverified.
The review attributes the 'food not specified' Pb 2.5 ppm and Cd 1.5 ppm values to the 2011 Regulations; these are not recorded as limits because they are secondary and possibly superseded.
